MUIPage

The MUIPage class is used to group UI elements into a page. You can add elements in C# through Children, or use MXML to load the page from a file.

Properties and Methods

  • Children: Contains the elements that belong to this page. An element can only belong to one page or window at a time.
  • Compile / CompileFile: Builds the page from MXML and returns whether compilation succeeded. If it fails, the previous page is kept.
  • BackendObjects: Contains application objects that MXML can use for data binding and callbacks. Add these before compiling the page.
  • CompilerOptions: Allows you to register custom types, choose how they are created, and set the base directory and include limits.

C# Example

Create the control and add it to the page's Children or the window's Elements collection. The Controls Overview lists the namespaces used by these examples.

MXML Example

Output Example

Notes

Each nested MUIPage has its own MXML name scope. You can use the same name in different pages, but names inside one page must be unique.

Children are positioned using their X, Y, Width and Height settings. They are not automatically placed below each other. For a layout with rows and columns, use GridContainer.

MUIPage does not receive focus itself. Focusing a page selects an eligible element inside it.

The common position, color, visibility and lifetime settings are inherited from UIElement. While attached to a running window, update the control on the UI thread.
